So Allah withheld the rain from them, and Nuh called them to believe so that Allah would lift the punishment from them; they believed and Allah lifted the punishment, but they returned to their disbelief. Allah revealed the Psalms to him; he was given a great kingdom and commanded by Allah to judge justly.

Solomon: Allah gave him knowledge and wisdom, taught him the speech of birds and animals and subjected winds and jinn to him. He had a story with the hoopoe, which told him of a kingdom in Yemen whose people worshipped the sun instead of Allah. Solomon sent to the queen of Sheba requesting faith, but she sent him gifts. He asked the jinn to bring her throne; when she came and found her throne, she believed in Allah.

Ayyub: descended from our master Abraham, one of the prophets receiving revelation. He possessed wealth and many children, but Allah tested him in all this and it was lost. His body suffered various afflictions, and his illness lasted eighteen years, during which people shunned him except his wife. She endured and worked to provide their daily food until Allah healed him and replaced everything in which he was tested. Thus Ayyub is cited as an example of patience and affliction. It is related that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will use Ayyub, peace be upon him, as an argument against those afflicted.

Yusuf: the son of our master Yaqub. He had eleven brothers, and his father loved him greatly. One night he saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him. He told his father what he saw, and his father told him not to relate it to his brothers. But the devil whispered to his brothers, and they agreed to throw him into the depths of a well and claimed a wolf had eaten him. Some Bedouins then passed him, took him and sold him for a paltry price. Egypt’s nobleman bought him and asked his wife to care for him. But she began seducing him; he refused, she plotted against him, and he entered prison. Allah then revealed his innocence and he left prison. The king appointed him over food affairs, which he managed well during the drought years. He then reunited with his brothers and parents; they fell prostrate before him, and his vision came true.

Musa is a messenger whom Allah the Exalted sent to Pharaoh and his people, and supported with two miracles: one of them is the staff that swallowed the serpents; the other was his hand, which he would put into his bosom and it would come out white without any blemish. Musa called to the oneness of Allah, so Pharaoh fought him and gathered the sorcerers against him to plot against him, but he defeated them by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Then Allah commanded him to leave Egypt with those who followed him, and Pharaoh pursued him with a great army; and when his followers thought they would be overtaken, Allah commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, so that it would be his salvation and the destruction of Pharaoh, whom Allah made a lesson for others.

Aaron: Moses' brother and companion in calling Pharaoh to believe in Allah, as he was eloquent and a speaker. Moses appointed him over his people when he went to meet Allah on Mount Tur. But the trial of Samiri occurred, leading the Israelites to worship a golden calf that lowed. Aaron called them back to worship Allah instead of the calf, but they grew arrogant. When Moses returned and saw what his people had come to, he reproached Aaron severely.

Then Allah commanded our master Abraham to build the Kaaba and raise the House's foundations: Ishmael brought stones while Abraham built until they completed it. He replied, 'Father, do what you are commanded; Allah willing, you will find me patient.' Allah ransomed him with a great sacrifice. Jonah sailed in a ship; when they were about to drown, they cast lots to decide which man to throw overboard. It fell three times to Jonah, who threw himself into the sea.
